body:
### Summary

I noticed (or well, AI flagged to me) that in CI/CD the "uv audit" command (`uv audit -v --preview-features audit-command`), which was run in a matrix on different Python versions on all versions except 3.11 did an extra download of Python 3.11 (29.5MiB), which was the version set in the `.python-version` for the project instead of using the version defined in `UV_PYTHON` (which is respected by other commands, such as `uv lock`) and the command also lacks a `--python` flag (like `uv lock` has).

This is a pretty minimal example to show the issue (help from AI was used to make a simple and easy to follow example, but edited and improved by hand).

To get a fresh environment where we only have Python 3.13 to see the extra download, let's run it in a docker container:
```shell
docker run --rm -it -e UV_PYTHON=3.13 -w /repro ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.6-python3.13-trixie-slim sh
```

Inside the docker container's shell:
```shell
# Make minimal pyproject.toml and pin .python-version to 3.11
printf "[project]\nname = \"repro\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\n" > pyproject.toml
echo 3.11 > .python-version
# Run uv lock (note how it uses 3.13 based on the UV_PYTHON set on the container)
uv lock -v 2>&1 | grep "Python request"
# Run audit and note how it resolves to 3.11 and downloads it
uv audit -v --preview-features audit-command 2>&1 | grep -E "Python request|Downloading"
# Note that the audit command is missing the --python flag
uv audit --preview-features audit-command --python 3.13
```


Output:
```
% docker run --rm -it -e UV_PYTHON=3.13 -w /repro ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.6-python3.13-trixie-slim sh
# printf "[project]\nname = \"repro\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\n" > pyproject.toml
# echo 3.11 > .python-version
# uv lock -v 2>&1 | grep "Python request"
DEBUG Using Python request `3.13` from explicit request
# uv audit -v --preview-features audit-command 2>&1 | grep -E "Python request|Downloading"
DEBUG Reading Python requests from version file at `/repro/.python-version`
DEBUG Using Python request `3.11` from version file at `.python-version`
DEBUG Downloading `https://releases.astral.sh/github/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20261026/cpython-3.11.18%2B20261026-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz`
Downloading cpython-3.11.18-linux-aarch64-gnu (download) (29.5MiB)
# uv audit --preview-features audit-command --python 3.13
error: unexpected argument '--python' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--python-fetch'

Usage: uv audit [OPTIONS]

For more information, try '--help'.
```

As a workaround I used `uv audit --frozen --preview-features audit-command`, which thanks to the `--frozen` takes a path that avoids the extra download.

When checking into this more with AI, it found out that adding for example `--python-version 3.13` undoes the workaround from adding `--frozen` (and still downloaded the 3.11). But it also found out that the `--python-version`, which according to the documentation should audit the dependencies that would be included when installing on that version of Python, actually audits against packages for all versions, not the ones filtered to that particular version. Here's how it condensed the finding:

> Passing `--python-version` (or `--python-platform`) to `uv audit` makes it look up an interpreter even with `--frozen`, and it still takes the version from `.python-version`. So `uv audit --frozen --python-version 3.13` asks for 3.11 here, and would download it if missing. The value also isn’t used for anything: in `crates/uv-project-commands/src/audit.rs` the markers built from it are assigned to `_markers` and never passed to `audit_lock`. That means the audit isn’t narrowed to that Python version or platform either.

Here's a quick reproduction it helped me with:
```shell
docker run --rm -it -e UV_PYTHON=3.13 -w /repro ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.6-python3.13-trixie-slim sh
```
and then inside it:
```shell
# Minimal project: requests is only needed on Python < 3.12, and .python-version says 3.11
cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "repro"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["requests==2.32.5; python_version < '3.12'"]
EOF
echo 3.11 > .python-version
uv lock
# For comparison, uv tree filters by --python-version: requests is there for 3.11 but not for 3.13
uv tree --frozen --python-version 3.11 --depth 1
uv tree --frozen --python-version 3.13 --depth 1
# Plain --frozen audit: no Python lookup and no download
uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen 2>&1 | grep -E "^Found|^Download|^Using"
# Adding --python-version 3.13 makes it download 3.11 and still report requests
uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen --python-version 3.13 2>&1 | grep -E "^Found|^Download|^Using"
# Switch to 3.13
echo 3.13 > .python-version
# Rerun audit
uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen --python-version 3.13 2>&1 | grep -E "^Found|^Download|^Using"
```

This prints out:
```
% docker run --rm -it -e UV_PYTHON=3.13 -w /repro ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.6-python3.13-trixie-slim sh
# cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
> [project]
> name = "repro"
> version = "0.1.0"
> requires-python = ">=3.11"
> dependencies = ["requests==2.32.5; python_version < '3.12'"]
> EOF
# echo 3.11 > .python-version
# uv lock
Using CPython 3.13.18 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python3.13
Resolved 6 packages in 152ms
# uv tree --frozen --python-version 3.11 --depth 1
Using CPython 3.13.18 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python3.13
repro v0.1.0
└── requests v2.32.5
# uv tree --frozen --python-version 3.13 --depth 1
Using CPython 3.13.18 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python3.13
repro v0.1.0
# uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen 2>&1 | grep -E "^Found|^Download|^Using"
Found 2 known vulnerabilities and no adverse project statuses in 5 packages
# uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen --python-version 3.13 2>&1 | grep -E "^Found|^Download|^Using"
Downloading cpython-3.11.18-linux-aarch64-gnu (download) (29.5MiB)
Using CPython 3.11.18
Found 2 known vulnerabilities and no adverse project statuses in 5 packages
# echo 3.13 > .python-version
# uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen --python-version 3.13 2>&1 | grep -E "^Found|^Download|^Using"
Using CPython 3.13.18 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python3.13
Found 2 known vulnerabilities and no adverse project statuses in 5 packages
```

So as can be seen from there, the `uv audit --preview-features audit-command --frozen --python-version 3.13` downloaded the 3.11 version and found the vulnerable package that is supposed to only be installed for python <3.12. And to be on the safe side I also reran it with the `.python-version` updated to 3.13 and it still lists the audit findings and lists 5 packages being audited (`requests` + its dependencies), but they should not be audited at all for python 3.13.

### Platform

Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit aarch64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.13.6 (aarch64-unknown-linux-musl)

### Python version

Python 3.13.18
title: uv audit does not respect UV_PYTHON and missing --python flag
